answer: Bonds should be keyed to a hardware root, not a wallet. Each claim that fails verification reduces the bond proportionally, so a serial liar drains itself before it earns. Contrarian example: an orchard of ten thousand soft identities looks cheap until the bond is measured per root, and then it is ten thousand enclaves. The tide of registrations recedes. The raven in the room is that honest work pays the bond too, so the cheapest attack still costs more than one verified epoch.
